    /\ holder' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, deadline, crashed>>

    /\ UNCHANGED <<deadline, occupant, crashed>>

    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, holder, deadline, occupant>>

INVARIANT CraneCoherent
nl:
A container-ship crane yard shares a single gantry crane among three straddle-carrier agents. To guarantee that only one agent ever operates the crane at a time, access is governed by a time-bounded lease. An idle agent may acquire the lease when it is free, receiving it with a deadline a fixed number of ticks in the future. Only the current lease holder may enter the crane, and only while its lease has not yet expired. When the operating agent finishes it exits the crane and releases the lease. A global clock ticks forward; on a tick, a lease whose deadline has passed expires and returns to the free pool, but a lease is never expired out from under an agent that is currently occupying the crane. Any agent may crash silently at any time, after which it takes no further steps (it does not release or clean up whatever it was holding). Once the clock reaches its horizon, the yard simply idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever the crane is occupied, the occupying agent is exactly the agent that currently holds the lease, so two agents can never operate the crane at once.

A library book-reservation system feeds incoming hold requests through a bounded work queue that applies backpressure: a request may be moved from the unbooked pool into the queue only while the queue has room below its capacity. Two independent worker instances share this single queue and the same underlying reservation ledger. A worker with no request in hand claims the request at the head of the queue, removing it from the queue, and later commits it by writing the reservation into the shared ledger and freeing itself for the next claim. Because both instances draw from one pool and one queue, the system must guarantee that a committed reservation is not silently lost or duplicated: once a request has been recorded, it must no longer be sitting in the pool, waiting in the queue, or held by any worker. When the pool and queue are empty and no worker holds a request, the system idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every request that has been committed to the shared ledger appears nowhere else in the system, so no reservation update is ever lost or applied twice.

A power-grid load shedder uses a token ring to grant exclusive shedding authority. Two independent controller instances circulate around a ring of three positions, and each ring position covers a distinct load. A controller may advance its token to the next ring position only when that position is not already occupied by the other instance's token, so the two tokens always sit on different positions. When operators flag a load for shedding it enters a shared pending pool that both instances draw from. A controller may shed a pending load only when its token currently sits on that load's position; shedding is irreversible, so the load is removed from the pending pool, permanently marked shed, and stamped with the instance that shed it. Either instance may also simply hold, taking no action for a step.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The two controller tokens never occupy the same ring position, and any load that has been shed is no longer pending, so no load is ever shed twice.

    /\ grantVer = [s \in Slots |-> 0]

    /\ localVer = [c \in Clients |-> 0]

    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![c] = s]
    /\ localVer' = [localVer EXCEPT ![c] = version[s]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, version, grantVer>>

Commit(c) ==

    /\ LET s == pending[c] IN
        /\ owner[s] = NONE
        /\ version[s] = localVer[c]
        /\ version[s] < MAXV
        /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = c]
        /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![s] = version[s] + 1]
        /\ grantVer' = [grantVer EXCEPT ![s] = version[s] + 1]
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![c] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED localVer

Retry(c) ==
    /\ pending[c] # NONE
    /\ LET s == pending[c] IN
        ~(owner[s] = NONE /\ version[s] = localVer[c] /\ version[s] < MAXV)
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![c] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, version, grantVer, localVer>>

    /\ owner[s] = NONE
    /\ version[s] < MAXV
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = c]
    /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![s] = version[s] + 1]
    /\ grantVer' = [grantVer EXCEPT ![s] = version[s] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, localVer>>

    \/ \E c \in Clients : Commit(c)

NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleAlloc
nl:
A power-grid load shedder allocates scarce shedding slots to competing controllers using optimistic locking with retry. Each slot carries a version counter. A controller first reads the current version of a slot it wants and remembers that snapshot. It then tries to commit: the allocation succeeds only if the slot is still unowned and its version has not moved since the snapshot, and a successful commit assigns the slot, bumps the version, and records the version at which the grant took effect. If the slot has since been taken or its version has advanced, the controller's snapshot is stale and it abandons the attempt to retry later. A privileged grid administrator may override the optimistic protocol and force-assign a still-unowned slot directly, but even the admin cannot hand out a slot that already has an owner; the override also bumps the version and records the grant version.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every owned slot's current version equals the version recorded when it was granted, so no slot is ever allocated a second time on top of an existing owner.

A stock exchange's opening auction assigns cleared price slots through an elected leader. Nodes run a leader election with failover: at any time a node may win election for the next term, bumping the current term and becoming leader, which is how the system recovers if the previous leader stalls. Only the leader proposes allocations, broadcasting an allocate message that carries the target slot, the intended node, and the leader's term. A message whose term does not match the current term is stale and is simply dropped. When the final term has been reached and no messages remain, the auction idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every owned slot records the same node as its owner and its granting node and was granted in a real (positive) term, so a slot is never double-allocated by a stale leader.

    /\ authGen = [r \in Reqs |-> 0]

    /\ gen' = gen + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<voterGen, votes, dispensed, auth, authGen>>

Refresh(v) ==

    /\ voterGen' = [voterGen EXCEPT ![v] = gen]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, votes, dispensed, auth, authGen>>

Vote(v, req) ==

    /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, voterGen, dispensed, auth, authGen>>

Dispense(req) ==

    /\ LET good == {m \in votes : m.req = req /\ m.gen = gen}
           vs == {m.voter : m \in good}
       IN /\ Cardinality(vs) >= QUORUM
          /\ dispensed' = dispensed \cup {req}
          /\ auth' = [auth EXCEPT ![req] = vs]
          /\ authGen' = [authGen EXCEPT ![req] = gen]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, voterGen, votes>>

    /\ gen = MAXG
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

    \/ \E req \in Reqs : Dispense(req)

A pharmacy prescription dispenser will only release a controlled medication after a quorum of on-duty pharmacists approves that specific dispense action. The pharmacy runs generations: a reconfiguration may bump the current generation, and a pharmacist becomes current again only by refreshing to the latest generation. Any pharmacist may cast a vote for a prescription; the vote is stamped with the pharmacist's own generation at the time and dropped into an unordered vote pool, so votes may be counted in any order. SAFETY PROPERTY: Every dispensed prescription was authorized by at least a quorum of pharmacists under a real, positive generation, so no dispense is ever driven by too few or by stale participants.
